subject: Platform Reliability Pulse — leadership comms & temporary role rotations
thread_summary: Draft and finalize a short leadership announcement about a week-long "pulse" on platform reliability, plus implement temporary role rotations to improve coverage and cross-team knowledge before QBR. Collect feedback and lock messaging for company-wide communication.
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, ops-consultant@exterra.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Platform Reliability Pulse — leadership comms & temporary role rotations

Hi all,

As we get closer to the QBR, I want to propose a short, focused "Platform Reliability Pulse" the week of Aug 12 — a coordinated effort to surface operational risks, validate runbooks, and give us a clean set of metrics for the QBR readout. My ask is twofold:

1) Leadership comms: draft a 2–3 paragraph announcement we can share with the org that explains the pulse intent, what teams will be involved, and high-level outcomes we expect (metrics and readouts). I attached a rough draft (pulse-comm-draft.docx).

2) Temporary role rotations: run a lightweight rotation across infra/platform leads for 2 weeks during the pulse window to improve coverage and force cross-pairing on runbooks and incident handoffs. I attached a short rationale (rotation-rationale.pdf).

Proposed owner for comms: Marissa (can you take the first pass?)
Proposed owner for rotations logistics: Karthik (can you outline ops owners and scheduling constraints?)
I'll loop in Soojin and Jonas for the QBR metrics tie-in.

Please review the attached comm draft and the rotation rationale and reply with edits or objections by end of day Monday (Aug 1) — I want to lock messaging and the rotation schedule by Tue Aug 2 so we can publish the calendar invite and update the runbook owners.

Key questions to consider in your responses:
- Should rotation length be 2 weeks or 3 weeks?
- Do we need to expand participation to Dedicated and Private platform squads?
- Any customer-facing risks we should call out in the comms (Claire from Acme is copied to flag anything that might impact her team)?

Thanks — this is intended to be a low-friction exercise but high value for the QBR.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
VP, Platform & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pulse-comm-draft.docx (document), rotation-rationale.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform Reliability Pulse — leadership comms & temporary role rotations

Mina — thanks for the draft and the ask. Quick notes: 

- I recommend 3-week rotations instead of 2. Two weeks is tight for knowledge transfer and any on-call handoffs; three gives a buffer to validate runbook changes.
- We should include Dedicated squad in the rotation schedule. They own a number of deployment and capacity playbooks that will affect the QBR metrics.
- I'll sketch a proposed owner matrix and scheduling constraints by Monday EOD.

No objections on the comms tone — short, direct, and non-alarming is the right approach. I'll coordinate with ops-consultant@exterra.com for any facilitation needs.

— Karthik
Head of Infrastructure

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jul 2028 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform Reliability Pulse — leadership comms & temporary role rotations

Thanks — I reviewed the pulse-comm-draft and made a light pass. Key edits: 
- Tightened the opening paragraph to call out the "three objectives" (validate runbooks, measure latency/resilience, and prioritize mitigations).
- Removed language that could sound customer-alarming (reworded "we will be testing incident responses" to "we will be validating and improving runbooks").
- Added a short FAQ blurb for engineering managers (who to contact, expected time commitment).

I've put the revised comm in the shared doc (link below) and exported a markdown stub attached (comm-v1.md). If we're moving to 3-week rotations (Karthik's suggestion), we should reflect that in the scheduling paragraph and add Dedicated squad explicitly.

Shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-platform-pulse-draft (internal)

Attaching comm-v1.md with inline comments. Will be available for edits Monday morning.

— Marissa
Director, Product Operations

Appreciate the quick turn. Summary / decisions:

- Rotation length: 3 weeks (agreed)
- Participation: include Dedicated squad + Platform + Infra; Will share a proposed owner matrix Monday (Karthik).
- Comms: Marissa's language looks good; incorporate the FAQ and the rewording to avoid customer alarm.

Next steps:
- Karthik: owner matrix + scheduling constraints (due Mon Aug 1, EOD)
- Marissa: finalize comm copy in the shared doc and attach the final version (due Mon Aug 1, EOD)
- I'll draft the calendar invites and the QBR metrics mapping once we have the owner matrix (target Tue Aug 2).

If there are objections to the plan or the wording, reply all. Otherwise I'll mark this approved for publication prep and we will publish a brief leadership note the morning of Aug 3 to give teams a heads-up.

— Mina
VP, Platform & Reliability
